topic: Pool-rank recovery of cell-type Poisson-CPCM effects from designed bulk mixtures. For K invariant type-specific nonnegative-integer count vectors, observe replicate raw-count pools with known integer composition matrix M, independent cells, no cross-cell interaction, and no unknown thinning or normalization. Prove that full column rank of M is necessary and sufficient for uniform recovery of all unrestricted type joint laws, fully crediting Shih--Hero's log-transform inversion and using positive independent-Poisson aliases for the converse. On a declared compact, causally sufficient, pairwise-identifiable nonlinear Poisson-CPCM subclass, transfer recovery to labeled type DAGs and fixed truncated-factorization intervention contrasts. Give a normwise lower-envelope stability theorem involving ||M+||, and, on a prespecified finite PGF grid, derive replicate-well delta covariance, sample-split graph selection, and pointwise sandwich-Wald inference under certified graph-separation and Jacobian margins. Consumer: Luo--Sun--Zhang's empirical bulk-gene causal-recoverability workflow, prospectively redesigned with linearly independent known-composition replicate pools. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The score-blind presolve derived the full-rank inverse and positive-Poisson converse, verified a nonlinear three-node CPCM witness with intervention contrasts 3 and 25, established normwise stability and cross-type/grid covariance, and proved existence of a separating finite grid for compact positive-polynomial Poisson DAG families from score-information positivity, signed-PGF uniqueness, and compactness. A 27-point pilot had component-Jacobian singular values 0.00326480 and 0.00262027; Shih--Hero and transform-GMM collisions, rank-deficient graph aliases, finite-grid nonparametric aliases, unknown channels, vanishing edges, and pooling attenuation were checked. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Produce an explicit certified grid with a positive wrong-graph score gap, uniform within-graph Jacobian lower bound, controlled PGF truncation, and useful propagated contrast precision over the compact parameter boxes. EARLY KILL TEST: For p=3, M=[[1,1],[1,2]], coefficients in [1/2,3], and grid {0.8,0.9,0.97}^3, certify separation from all 24 incorrect single-type DAGs and both witness Jacobians by interval/global optimization; an exact collision kills that protocol, and failure of useful precision after one prespecified grid refinement stops the practical launch. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/eid_bulk_poolrank_cpcm_effect.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For p=3, M=[[1,1],[1,2]], coefficient boxes [1/2,3], and the prespecified grid {0.8,0.9,0.97}^3, does there exist a machine-checkable positive lower bound on every wrong-DAG Poisson-CPCM PGF score, simultaneously with positive lower bounds on both true-model Jacobian singular values and a uniform PGF-tail truncation bound?

source_refs.claim: Aggregation is generally lossy for causal recovery; nonlinear cellular mechanisms fall outside the paper's affine recoverability conditions.
source_refs.author: Gongxu Luo, Boyang Sun, Kun Zhang

source_refs.claim: Poisson CPCMs are generically graph-identifiable from the full direct observational law, with an explicitly characterized exceptional bivariate family.
source_refs.author: Juraj Bodik, Valérie Chavez-Demoulin

source_refs.claim: Introduces cumulant-generating-function-domain inversion of independent additive components from known aggregate paths.
source_refs.author: Meng-Fu Shih, Alfred O. Hero III

open_problems.why_unsolved: Bodik and Chavez-Demoulin separate CPCM directions using the complete type-level law, while Shih and Hero invert complete transforms of independent additive components. Neither result supplies a finite evaluation set or a quantitative margin after pool inversion. The population noncoincidence step must therefore be replaced by rigorous global minimization of each wrong-graph finite-grid discrepancy over compact parameter boxes, together with interval bounds for the smallest singular value and omitted PGF tail. Searches for designed bulk mixtures combined with CPCMs, pooled-count PGFs combined with causal-DAG recovery, and known-composition causal graph recovery found no occupied target-method pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computer-assisted theorem giving explicit constants gamma>0, kappa>0, and epsilon_tail for the stated M, parameter boxes, and grid—respectively a uniform wrong-graph score gap, uniform within-graph Jacobian lower bound, and truncation error smaller than the certified gap—or an exact parameter collision disproving the protocol.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from the empirical appeal of bulk expression to aggregation-induced failure of causal recovery and the need for explicit additional assumptions.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Bulk profiling remains attractive -> ordinary aggregation destroys nonlinear causal information -> designed independent mixtures may restore type laws -> restoration must be certified on the actual finite PGF grid

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the sufficient-statistic incompatibility proof for reverse CPCM factorizations, replacing full-law inequality by a finite-grid discrepancy whose infimum is certified over every wrong-graph parameter box.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the graph-identification mechanism that the finite PGF score must preserve quantitatively after unpooling.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine exact-rational Smale-alpha certification of candidate zeros with interval branch-and-bound excluding unsampled compact boxes and certifying Jacobian nonsingularity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required resolution is a proof-producing certificate that nonlinear score equations have no wrong-graph zero and that true-model roots are regular.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt characteristic-function mixture GMM after known linear aggregation, including covariance weighting of transform moments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It estimates independent component distributions from known aggregate transforms, matching the inverse layer that precedes finite-grid CPCM fitting.

open_problems.open_problem: Under a certified finite-grid graph gap and Jacobian margin, can replicate-well empirical PGFs yield sample-split graph-consistent estimation and pointwise sandwich-Wald inference for fixed truncated-factorization Poisson-CPCM intervention contrasts, with full same-well cross-grid covariance and explicit ||M^+|| variance amplification?

source_refs.claim: Identifies independent component distributions from Y=AX and estimates them by transform-based GMM, but does not study causal graph selection or intervention contrasts.
source_refs.author: Aiyou Chen, Jin Cao, Tian Bu

source_refs.claim: Establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and covariance-optimal weighting for finite or continuum-indexed moment conditions.
source_refs.author: Marine Carrasco, Jean-Pierre Florens

source_refs.claim: Provides consistent CPCM graph-recovery algorithms for direct random samples but no pooled-transform sandwich law for post-selection causal contrasts.
source_refs.author: Juraj Bodik, Valérie Chavez-Demoulin

open_problems.why_unsolved: Transform-GMM theory gives a limit law for a fixed moment model, and CPCM work gives graph consistency from direct observations, but their composition is not automatic. Empirical-PGF values at different grid points from the same well are correlated; inversion couples inferred type transforms through M^+; graph selection is discrete; and the intervention contrast is a nonlinear functional of recovered conditional laws. The missing proof step is a joint replicate-well CLT passed through linear unpooling, within-graph estimation, and the contrast delta map, with sample splitting and the certified score gap making the selected graph asymptotically fixed.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit estimator and theorem stating graph-selection consistency and a pointwise normal limit for the intervention-contrast estimator, with a consistently estimable sandwich covariance containing all cross-grid and cross-type terms and a normwise upper envelope proportional to ||M^+||^2.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates distributional inference from inaccessible components observed only through known aggregate measurements and separates identification from transform-based estimation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Component laws are scientifically relevant but inaccessible -> aggregate measurements create an inverse problem -> transform moments make estimation tractable -> causal consumers additionally require graph-safe contrast uncertainty

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over the covariance-operator GMM linearization and optimal-weighting proof, specialized to the finite vector of within-well PGF evaluations before applying M^+ and the contrast gradient.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired sandwich law is a transform-moment GMM limit with a non-diagonal covariance kernel.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its transform-domain component-distribution estimator for known aggregate matrices while retaining the empirical-transform covariance rather than treating grid coordinates independently.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its observation equation is the closest statistical inverse analogue to known-composition count pools.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the CPCM graph-separation characterization to define the discrete selection event that sample splitting and a positive score margin make negligible in the second-stage limit law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the identifiable graph layer on which the truncated-factorization contrast is evaluated.

open_problems.open_problem: Among nonnegative-integer composition matrices and replicate allocations obeying fixed total-cell and well budgets, which full-rank designs minimize the worst-case asymptotic variance of a prespecified Poisson-CPCM intervention contrast while preserving a positive finite-grid wrong-graph separation margin?

source_refs.claim: Shows that measurement design is often neglected in aggregate tomography and optimizes path-probe allocation using Fisher-information criteria.
source_refs.author: Ting He, Chang Liu, Ananthram Swami, Don Towsley, Theodoros Salonidis, Andrei Iu Bejan, Paul Yu

source_refs.claim: Finds that the mixture weight matrix is the most important factor in RNA-seq deconvolution performance and notes that it had been overlooked.
source_refs.author: Haijing Jin, Zhandong Liu

source_refs.claim: Shows why ordinary bulk aggregation cannot generally preserve nonlinear causal relations, motivating prospective rather than inherited mixture designs.
source_refs.author: Gongxu Luo, Boyang Sun, Kun Zhang

open_problems.why_unsolved: Full column rank settles only qualitative recoverability. Jin and Liu empirically connect deconvolution performance to the weight matrix but treat it as uncontrolled, while He et al. optimize continuous probe allocations for network likelihoods rather than integer biological compositions, nonlinear CPCM graph margins, or intervention contrasts. The information criterion must instead propagate replicate-PGF covariance through M^+, the within-DAG Jacobian inverse, and the contrast gradient while treating graph separation as a hard design constraint. Searches found mixture-control experiments and network-tomography design separately, but no optimal known-composition design for causal-DAG contrasts.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A c- or E-optimal design theorem characterizing, or giving a provably near-optimal algorithm for, the integer matrix M and well allocations minimizing compact-box worst-case contrast variance subject to rank, cell-budget, and certified graph-gap constraints.

writing_exemplar.why: Its aggregation warning motivates changing data acquisition prospectively instead of applying another downstream algorithm to irreversibly coarsened samples.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Routine bulk aggregation loses nonlinear causal structure -> independent known-composition pools can restore information -> full rank alone may be numerically useless -> design compositions for the target contrast and graph margin

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt Fisher-information A-, D-, and weighted-design criteria and the proof linking allocation to attainable asymptotic covariance, replacing paths by integer mixture rows and link parameters by the causal-contrast gradient.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems prospectively allocate aggregate measurements to stabilize recovery of inaccessible component parameters.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the optimal transform-GMM covariance operator to derive the design-dependent information matrix before applying the contrast delta method.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The design objective must use the correlated PGF-moment covariance rather than only the condition number of M.

method_exemplars.technique: Translate CPCM direction incompatibility into a design-dependent minimum-separation constraint.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The optimal design must retain graph identification as well as reduce contrast variance.

open_problems.open_problem: When nominal pool compositions or type-specific capture efficiencies are known only to lie in calibrated intervals, what is the sharp identified set for a fixed Poisson-CPCM truncated-factorization intervention contrast, and at what uncertainty radius does a full-rank nominal design cease to distinguish competing labeled DAGs?

source_refs.claim: Known RNA mixtures reveal systematic measurement bias, and poly-A enrichment requires component-specific correction before the linear mixture model is valid.
source_refs.author: Jerod Parsons, Sarah Munro, P. Scott Pine, Jennifer McDaniel, Michele G. Mehaffey, Marc Salit

source_refs.claim: Documents strong effects of weight-matrix geometry, measurement scale, and unknown biological content on RNA-seq deconvolution.
source_refs.author: Haijing Jin, Zhandong Liu

source_refs.claim: Derives identification regions and confidence sets for latent distributions when the linear measurement-error matrix is restricted but not known exactly.
source_refs.author: Francesca Molinari

open_problems.why_unsolved: The exact pool-rank argument treats M and the count channel as known, whereas mixture-control studies show that enrichment and component-specific RNA content perturb the effective mixing operator. Once the operator ranges over a calibrated set, applying one pseudoinverse is invalid and graph identity can vary across admissible channels. Molinari's linear-system identified regions do not include nonlinear PGF factorization or graph selection. The missing step is joint optimization over admissible channels, type laws, and CPCM DAG factorizations while enforcing observed pooled-PGF compatibility; the web scan found no such bounds for causal intervention contrasts.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp optimization characterization of lower and upper intervention-contrast endpoints over all calibrated composition or capture matrices and compatible Poisson-CPCM laws, plus the breakdown radius where the identified DAG set first becomes non-singleton and valid confidence sets for the endpoints.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames known mixtures as process controls and makes failure of exact linear response concrete through protocol-induced, component-specific bias.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Known mixtures should produce predictable linear signals -> sequencing protocols introduce component-specific departures -> exact inversion becomes assumption-sensitive -> report sharp causal-contrast bounds under calibrated departures

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the simultaneous-equation representation with a set-valued error matrix, optimization of functionals over compatible latent distributions, and confidence-set construction for identified-region endpoints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems replace inversion of a known linear observation operator by an identified set over a restricted operator family.

method_exemplars.technique: Carry over robust optimization over a user-specified measurement-noise set, imposing PGF compatibility and CPCM factorization constraints instead of a noisy-covariate adjustment equation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how bounded measurement uncertainty can produce causal-effect bounds instead of an unjustified corrected point estimate.

method_exemplars.technique: Use the exceptional-family characterization to determine whether each admissible recovered type law supports one or multiple CPCM directions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sharp contrast bounds require tracking graph ambiguity induced by channel uncertainty, not only uncertainty in the recovered distribution.

literature_map:
Shih--Hero (2001, ICASSP) pioneered cumulant-generating-function inversion for independent additive components observed through known aggregate paths.
Shih--Hero (2003, IEEE TSP) moved network-delay tomography toward finite-mixture likelihoods, emphasizing estimation rather than a universal law-recovery frontier.
Chen--Cao--Bu (2010, IEEE TSP; arXiv:0712.3618) proves distributional identification up to shifts in network tomography and develops characteristic-function GMM.
Carrasco--Florens (2000, Econometric Theory) supplies consistency, asymptotic normality, and covariance-optimal weighting for finite or continuum transform moments.
Park--Raskutti (2015, NeurIPS) identifies directly observed Poisson DAGs through overdispersion scoring and gives a polynomial-time learner.
Park--Park (2019, JMLR) gives high-dimensional Poisson-SEM graph recovery with an explicit sample-size requirement, again for direct samples.
Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin (2025, JMLR; arXiv:2303.15376) establishes CPCM identifiability, including Poisson exceptional reverse-factorization families, and consistent graph algorithms.
Luo--Sun--Zhang (2026; arXiv:2606.00568) shows ordinary bulk aggregation preserves its causal consistency notions only with linear aggregation and affine mechanisms, motivating prospective information-restoring designs.
Parsons et al. (2015, BMC Genomics) use known biological mixtures as process controls and show that poly-A enrichment can create component-specific bias requiring correction.
RNA-seq Mixology (2017, Nucleic Acids Research; DOI:10.1093/nar/gkw1063) demonstrates replicated known-proportion designs and documents attenuation as mixtures become compositionally similar.
Zaitsev et al. (2019, Nature Communications; DOI:10.1038/s41467-019-09990-5) warns that RNA fractions need not equal cell fractions because total RNA content varies by type.
Jin--Liu (2021, Genome Biology) identifies weight-matrix geometry as an overlooked dominant determinant of deconvolution performance and studies unknown-content failures.
He et al. (2015, ACM SIGMETRICS) optimizes aggregate-tomography probe allocation by Fisher information; no located paper transfers that logic to pooled causal-DAG contrasts.
Molinari (2008, Journal of Econometrics) and Guo et al. (2022, CLeaR) provide adjacent partial-identification machinery for uncertain measurement operators, but not pooled PGFs or graph-dependent intervention functionals.
Hauenstein--Sottile (2012, ACM TOMS; arXiv:1011.1091) provides proof-producing numerical certification machinery; no located application certifies finite-grid separation of compact Poisson-CPCM DAG families.
